unit.label: -like
unit.mentor_note: Like is the most honest of the resemblance suffixes: it says plainly that the thing is not the thing. Childlike and childish both mean "like a child", and the difference between them is the whole of tone.

members.meaning: having the innocence of a child
resembling a god in power or beauty
competent and efficient, though not inspired

discovery.understand_note: Like flags a comparison, not an identity. Set childlike (warm) beside childish (dismissive) and you can see how much a suffix alone can carry.

applies.prompt: Knowing -like means resembling, what is a reviewer saying when they call a novel workmanlike?

options.text: It is competent and solidly made, but not inspired
